subject: Micronix Dedicated SKU: tiling/fallback & memory-latency rebalancing
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Liu <sara.liu@micronix.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Micronix Dedicated SKU: tiling/fallback & memory-latency rebalancing

Sara —

Thanks for the time earlier. As promised, attached is a pragmatic SKU plan that balances Micronix's high-throughput daytime workloads with the memory-heavy nightly batch jobs you described. Key highlights below so it's quick to scan: 

- Recommended primary pool: mixed A100 (40%) + L4 (40%) with a small H100 reserve (20%) for peak low-latency, long-context requests.
- Rationale: A100 gives consistent FP16 throughput for your mid-length sessions, L4 is cost-efficient for short-turnaround interactive queries (low latency), H100 reserved for 1) large context generation (>64k tokens) and 2) model variants with high memory KV cache.
- Tiling/slotting approach: prefer fractional tiling on A100 for throughput bursts; reserve full-slot H100 nodes that can be pre-warmed for HH requests.
- Fallthrough: when H100 capacity is saturated, requests tagged as high-memory will either 1) queue briefly (50–200ms target) or 2) fallback to quantized A100 variant with slight quality trade-off.

I've included a lightweight cost/latency sensitivity matrix in the spreadsheet (micronix_sku_matrix_v2.xlsx) and a one-page latency summary (h100-a100-l4_latency_summary.pdf).

Next steps I recommend:
1) You and procurement review the spreadsheet and mark any absolute memory-floor jobs.
2) We run a 48–72hr pilot with a 1:1 replay of a representative traffic slice to validate cache-hit assumptions.
3) If pilot looks good, we produce a capacity commit that stages A100 and L4 immediately and spins H100 in a reserved pool for canary runs.

If you'd like, we can sketch two contract options: Laterally balanced (lower monthly commit, more burst) vs SLA-focused (larger reserve, lower tail latency guarantees).

Happy to jump on a call next week with Kimberly and Dev to walk the matrix.

Best,

Ben Carter
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0137

Attachments: micronix_sku_matrix_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet), h100-a100-l4_latency_summary.pdf (PDF summary)

From: Sara Liu <sara.liu@micronix.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Micronix Dedicated SKU: tiling/fallback & memory-latency rebalancing

Ben —

Thanks, this is a useful starting point. A few clarifying items from our engineering and procurement teams: 

1) Nightly batch jobs require >=384GB GPU RAM per job or they OOM; can you confirm which SKUs support this without tiling?
2) What's the expected token latency hit if we fallback from H100 to a quantized A100 variant (any empirical number you can share)?
3) Procurement wants two commit options with clear monthly unit economics (we'll need runway numbers for 12-month vs 36-month).

Also looping in Liam from infrastructure (cc'd) — he may ask for a short runbook for graceful degradation during spikes.

Regards,
Sara
Director, AI Infrastructure — Micronix

Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 08:20:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Micronix Dedicated SKU: tiling/fallback & memory-latency rebalancing

Ben / team —

Quick internal read and proposed answers to Sara's questions before we reply: 

1) 384GB requirement: only H100 (full 80GBxN with NVLink or partitioned H100 NVL) can support a single-job non-tiling footprint at that floor if N>=5 (5x80GB contiguous or NVLink fabric). A100 80GB is close but we'd need aggressive tiling across 6+ slots and we'd still see higher tail latency. Practically: to guarantee <OOT, recommend a small reserved H100 pool sized for concurrent nightly jobs (suggest 6x H100 for your base).

2) Latency hit when falling back H100->quantized-A100: measured in our labs using your model family (GPT-style, 65k context) shows 8–15% increase in median token latency and a 4–7% drop in n-gram fidelity on heavy-attention passes. We can provide the raw bench logs if they want. For many customer workloads this is acceptable when weighed against the delta in unit cost.

3) Commit options: I'll sketch numbers with Dev's input — two quick frames:
   - 12-mo balanced: commit to 60% of projected peak with on-demand burst for the rest. Lower up-front but higher unit price.
   - 36-mo SLA-focused: commit to 90% of peak, includes H100 reserve, reduced per-token price, and 99.9th percentile latency SLA.

Operational runbook notes: if H100 headroom drops below 20%, route new high-memory sessions to a short pre-warm queue (max 300ms) and parallelize checkpointing to avoid queue buildup. We'll add those steps to the pilot checklist.

I'll pull together an ops-sensitive cost sheet (Excel) and a short fallthrough runbook. Dev — can you validate the H100 concurrency math and add any limits around NVLink fabric aggregation?

-Kim

Kimberly Park
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Micronix Dedicated SKU: tiling/fallback & memory-latency rebalancing

Sara / Liam —

Thanks for the quick questions — appreciated. We've attached a short appendix and an ops runbook. Quick answers and actions below: 

- Memory floor: we recommend reserving 6x H100 nodes (NVLink fabric) to satisfy the 384GB per-job requirement without tiling. Those nodes will be in a hot standby pool and can be pre-warmed overnight for your batch window.
- Latency delta: expect median token latency +10% when falling back to quantized A100 in our representative tests. We'll include the bench logs in the drive folder.
- Commit frames: Kimberly and Dev are preparing a detailed 12-month vs 36-month pricing sheet; I'll route that to procurement by EOD tomorrow.

Attached: micronix_sku_matrix_v2.xlsx (updated with H100 reserve row) and h100-a100-l4_latency_summary.pdf (bench logs referenced). Also added a short fallthrough-runbook.md in Drive link.

If Micronix agrees, let's schedule the 48–72hr pilot for July 20–22 (we'll need a replay slice and a small API key with tokenized traffic). I'll coordinate operational playbooks with Liam.

Best,
Ben
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
